correctness.rationale: Every matching of the Fano incidence graph is a permutation satisfying seven incidence tests, so all 7!=5040 permutations can be exhausted. An alternating six-cycle flip changes exactly three row assignments; conversely any two allowed permutations differing at exactly three positions differ by a single alternating hexagon (girth six rules out 4-cycles). An independent DFS matching generator and explicit six-cycle generator gave 24 matchings, 28 hexagons and 84 flips, with all 576 ordered vertex pairs satisfying the listed intersection parameters. A checked vertex permutation phi matches every one of the 576 entries of the exact 24-by-24 published Klein adjacency matrix, so identity does not rely on an unproved uniqueness of intersection arrays. The independent computation also found eight disjoint one-factorization triples, distance three within fibers, and exactly one outgoing edge to each other fiber per vertex. The finite enumeration is exhaustive for this fully specified finite graph.

value.rationale: The full configuration-space graph of local perfect-matching moves is a natural object. An explicit identification with a classical distance-regular graph, including the antipodal correspondence with all one-factorizations, is a substantive structural classification beyond the already-known number of perfect matchings, despite concerning only one canonical finite incidence graph.
